name: Educational research association launched by AKU-IED

content.title: Educational research association launched by AKU-IED
content.summary: The international conference on 'Quality in Education: Teaching and Leadership in Challenging Times' organised by Aga Khan University Institute for Educational Development (AKU-IED) concluded successfully at the Institute's Karimabad campus in Karach

media.alt: Educational research association launched by AKU-IED

content.text: The international conference on 'Quality in Education: Teaching and Leadership in Challenging Times' organised by Aga Khan University Institute for Educational Development (AKU-IED) concluded successfully at the Institute's Karimabad campus in Karachi. Three days of deliberations and discussions by national and international researchers, academics and educationists led to several outcomes including the identification of areas and issues for research and dissemination at future conferences.

A significant outcome of the conference was the launch of Pakistan Educational Research Association (PERA) on the final day of the conference. The launching ceremony was attended by a large group of educationists, academics and researchers from private and government institutions, including Dr Hafiz Iqbal, Director, Institute of Education and Research, University of Punjab; and Prof Noor-ul-Haq, Director, Provincial Institute of Teacher Education (PITE), Balochistan.

Speaking at the launching ceremony of PERA, AKU-IED Director Dr Muhammad Memon described it as a 'community of researchers'. Noting that promotion of research and scholarship was part of AKU's strategic vision, he said: "It is in fulfilment of this vision that the University is committed to support the creation of PERA which would be a national resource in educational research for Pakistan."

The Head of Research and Policy Studies at AKU-IED, Dr Anjum Halai, provided an overview of and rationale for PERA. She said that PERA aimed to sustain and promote a vibrant educational research culture in Pakistan; enhance the impact of research on policy and practice; provide a forum for educationists and educational researchers to share research findings and best practices; disseminate research findings and encourage scholarly inquiry; and provide opportunities for members to build and enhance their research capacity. Although AKU-IED would support PERA in the initial phase, it would ultimately become an independent body with membership representing public and private sectors, she added.

The conference also resulted in a set of papers that will be compiled as conference proceedings. This would be a significant resource as it would document a large number of papers on the topic of quality education with specific reference to issues pertaining to Pakistan and the developing world.

AKU's academic, research and service activities - encompassing ten teaching sites in seven countries of South Asia, Eastern Africa and Europe - are targeted at helping the developing world, and especially the Muslim Ummah, to progress in areas of education and health.
